title: Gaza: The Fragile Anatomy of a Human and International Crisis
author: Carlos Calles
content:

issues published by the Frente Amplio de Mexicanos y Migrantes.[Read and

“The nightmare in Gaza is more than a humanitarian crisis; it is a crisis of
humanity.”

— António Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations

What is happening in Gaza cannot be ignored; these are crimes against humanity
being perpetrated by Zionism, a true genocide. And although its main architect
has been taken to the UN podium to defend his position, it is undeniable that
Milekowsky is a true murderer and must pay for his crimes.

Israel is launching a brutal offensive against Palestine, in the Gaza Strip
and in other nations. This is why several countries have filed charges against
this individual before the International Criminal Court for his arrest.
Perhaps the most prominent is Turkey, since Milekowsky will be arrested if he
sets foot on Turkish soil.

A brutal humanitarian crisis, murders, famine, and veritable extermination
camps in the year 2026 are irrefutable proof that Israel is a genocidal state,
nothing more, nothing less.

The impact of the conflict on the civilian population is reflected in record-
breaking figures for victimization. At the close of the three-year assessment
window in October 2026, the accumulated records confirm more than 73,000
deaths and over 170,000 injuries in the Gaza Strip, having surpassed the
initial figures of 41,000 and 42,000 deaths documented during the first year
of hostilities.

![Gaza: The Fragile Anatomy of a Human and International
Crisis](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/ltam-
nov26-05-body-p21.jpg)Illustration: _Let 's Talk About Migration_, November
2026

Several technical reports presented to the United Nations Security Council
confirm that nearly 70% of the fatalities are women and children. This pattern
is explained by the continued use of heavy bombing and armed drones in densely
populated urban areas and near healthcare facilities.

Among the documented indicators and factual data, a cumulative increase of
over 41,000, 42,000, and 73,000 deaths in the general population between 2023
and 2026 stands out, as well as a total number of injuries ranging from over
96,000 to over 170,000. Furthermore, children and women constitute
approximately 70% of the total fatalities. Regarding PRCS medical personnel,
51 members were killed (31 on duty, of which 29 occurred in Gaza and 2 in the
West Bank, and 20 off duty), in addition to 6 MDA first responders killed
during the initial emergency deployments. Finally, regarding emergency care in
Rafah, in May 2025 more than 3,400 patients were treated in the context of 21
mass casualty events due to fire and shrapnel.

The work of rescue personnel has been carried out under extremely dangerous
conditions. The Palestinian Red Crescent Society (PRCS) reports 51 members
killed, 31 of whom died in the line of duty. Similarly, Magen David Adom (MDA)
recorded the loss of 6 rescuers in the initial hours of the response to the
October 2023 attack.

By May 2025, the establishment of new food distribution points led to spikes
in mass trauma: the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) Field
Hospital in Rafah treated more than 3,400 people in that month alone following
21 violent incidents involving firearms and explosions in the aid access
lines.

## Mass Displacement and Destruction of Civil Infrastructure

More than 90% of Gaza's population, between 1.8 and 2 million people, has been
forcibly displaced, in many cases repeatedly, up to six times. Among the most
significant displacements was the evacuation of one million people from the
Rafah area, which began in May 2024.

![Gaza: The Fragile Anatomy of a Human and International
Crisis](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/ltam-
nov26-05-body-p22.jpg)Illustration: _Let 's Talk About Migration_, November
2026

Living conditions at the end of 2026 remain precarious. Among the main
difficulties is the accelerated deterioration of shelters, where temporary
tents completely degrade after six months exposed to the elements, forcing the
use of flour sacks as barriers against winter flooding. Adding to this is the
blockade of materials, as Israeli authorities maintain restrictions on the
entry of basic construction supplies such as cement, wood, and metal sheets.
Furthermore, a severe impact is evident in the West Bank, where international
organizations have issued warnings following the displacement of 36,000
people, highlighting the risk of permanent demographic changes.

## The Socioeconomic and Infrastructural Impact

The scale of military operations has irreversibly altered the urban geography
of the territory: an estimated 23 million tons of rubble are scattered
throughout the Gaza Strip; assessments by multilateral agencies put the
capital needed for physical and institutional reconstruction at $70 billion;
the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) points to a 69-year setback in
human development indicators, along with a 35.1% drop in GDP in 2024; and
nearly 600 attacks against health infrastructure have been recorded, leaving
key complexes such as Al-Shifa Hospital out of service.

## Food Insecurity and the Declaration of Famine

The ongoing blockade transformed supply difficulties into a widespread
nutritional crisis. During the acute phase between 2024 and 2025, 100% of the
population was affected by acute food insecurity, with child deaths from
malnutrition recorded from March 2024 onward. During this period, less than
50% of missions to the north were approved, and a total blockade of deliveries
was in place for 11 weeks. This situation led to the formal declaration of
famine in the Gaza Governorate (Gaza City) by the Integrated Food Security
Phase Classification (IPC) on August 22, 2025.

By 2026, the access crisis was exacerbated by a severe international funding
shortfall. The World Food Programme's (WFP) budget was cut by more than half,
forcing it to reduce its coverage by a third and decrease hot meals from
250,000 to 150,000 per day. This reduction left 500,000 people without food
assistance and 200,000 in need of urgent nutritional intervention. UN special
rapporteurs and experts have described these measures as the use of hunger as
a weapon of war.

![Gaza: The Fragile Anatomy of a Human and International
Crisis](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/ltam-
nov26-05-body-p23.jpg)Illustration: _Let 's Talk About Migration_, November
2026

## The International Judicial Front: Lawsuits and Rulings

The legal dimension of the crisis has led to proceedings of global scope
before the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and various multilateral
organizations.

In the context of South Africa's case against Israel, initiated in January
2024, the ICJ ordered binding provisional measures to demand the prevention of
acts of genocide and to guarantee access to basic assistance. Also, in March
2024, Nicaragua filed a case against Germany for alleged complicity in
violations of the Genocide Convention through military supplies. Subsequently,
in its mandate on humanitarian aid in October 2025, the ICJ determined that
Israel is legally obligated to allow the unconditional entry of UN-coordinated
aid. For their part, various reports by UN experts, including those prepared
by Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese (2024, 2026) and the Independent
International Commission of Inquiry (October 2024), concluded that there were
reasonable grounds to suspect genocidal acts and the crime against humanity of
"extermination."

The timeline of international intervention began on December 29, 2023, when
South Africa initiated genocide proceedings before the International Court of
Justice (ICJ) against Israel. The court issued its first binding provisional
measures on January 26, 2024. Subsequently, on March 25, 2024, the Security
Council demanded an immediate ceasefire during Ramadan. On April 23, 2024, the
Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR)
requested investigations following the discovery of mass graves in hospitals,
and on October 10, 2024, the UN Commission on Human Rights formally declared
the commission of extermination. Finally, on October 22, 2025, the ICJ issued
a mandate demanding the unconditional opening of aid.

Despite the ceasefire agreement reached on October 10, 2025 —which facilitated
the release and handover of 1,808 Palestinian detainees through the ICRC—,
operational stability has not been consolidated.

By the end of 2026, United Nations representatives warn that the risk of a
full-scale resumption of fighting is high. In the year following the
ceasefire, approximately 1,500 additional deaths were recorded, including 340
children. The stalemate in disarmament, troop withdrawal, and the
establishment of a unified administration has frozen reconstruction plans,
highlighting a critical gap between the mandates of international justice and
the reality on the ground.
